properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-19 for Mission Bay's third real-buildings pass (remaining uncovered footprints inside the official Mission Bay North/South redevelopment-area boundary): The Mission Creek Park Pavilion, an SF Recreation and Parks Department building at 290 Channel St within Mission Creek Park (12 acres), with floor-to-ceiling windows and two patios overlooking Mission Creek, available for café/recreational use; adjacent to the Channel Street Dog Park. Confirmed not to overlap the already-tracked Mission Creek Park boundary polygon (mission_bay_creek_park.geojson). 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: corrections: (1) the '12 acres' figure for Mission Creek Park is not stated by any cited source (SF Rec & Park's pavilion page, the missionbayparks.com venue page, OSM way 188854480) and should be disregarded. (2) SF Rec & Park's page says it assumed maintenance of 'nearby' Mission Bay Kids Park and Channel Street Dog Park, not that the pavilion is adjacent to the dog park; and 'available for café/recreational use' is not on that page: Mission Local (Sept 5, 2026) reports the building was built as a café space and a coffee tenant has now opened there. 2026-10-12 accuracy audit follow-up: correction to the 2026-09-29 note above, which said 'available for café/recreational use' is not on SF Rec & Park's pages. It is not on the pavilion page (sfrecpark.org/1704), but Rec & Park's own request-for-proposals page for the pavilion (https://sfrecpark.org/1823/Mission-Creek-Pavilion-RFP) says: 'The Department seeks a lessee to operate a café or recreational concession that fits well with the neighborhood.' (page also says 'Request for Proposals issued – Wednesday, February 26, 2025'). That wording is a use the Department solicited (RFP issued 2025-02-26), not a description of how the building is used now, so the ADDED sentence above ('available for café/recreational use') is out of date: Mission Local (Sept 5, 2026) says the building was built as a café space and that 'On Aug. 1, 2026, it finally opened for business' as the first San Francisco location of Zocalo Coffee. The RFP page is added to source_doc_urls. No change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type.
